heard: NASA completely forgot about hundreds of trees grown from space seeds. In 1971, Apollo 14 astronaut Stuart Roosa carried the seeds while orbiting the moon. Despite a vacuum chamber accident on Earth, the U.S. Forest Service successfully grew the seedlings. Around 1976, these saplings were planted worldwide to celebrate the American bicentennial. However, NASA failed to keep any official records tracking their locations. In 1996, a third grade teacher named Joan Goble found one at an Indiana camp. When she emailed NASA, shocked scientists realized they didn't even know the program existed. Planetary scientist Dave Williams dug through old archives to rebuild the history from scratch. A public search continues to locate these forgotten living monuments.
